rows.head: Ehlers reaches 600 points, but the Hurricanes lose
rows.story: Talk about a finish. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins played his first game of the season, after missing the first nine. Leon Draisaitl opened the scoring for the Oilers on the power play midway through the first.

rows.head: Four points for Fox, but the Rangers lose
rows.story: Easton Cowan opened the scoring for the Maple Leafs less than two minutes in, but Mika Zibanejad tied it 1-1 for the Rangers just over four minutes later. Teddy Blueger scored his first goal for Toronto less than five minutes later to put the Maple Leafs ahead 2-1. The second period was a wild one.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: The Kraken beat the Mammoth
rows.story: Jordan Eberle got the scoring started for the Kraken early in the first, but Vincent Trocheck tied it up for Utah on the power play late in the period. Matty Beniers put the Kraken ahead 2-1 on the power play 26 seconds later. Brandon Montour made it 3-1 on the power play early in the second.
rows.calls: Three of four preview calls held

rows.head: Robertson reaches 500 points as the Stars beat the Jets
rows.story: What a finish. Wyatt Johnston opened the scoring for the Stars early in the second, with Jason Robertson picking up his 500th NHL point on the assist. Gabriel Vilardi and Kyle Connor scored less than two minutes apart midway through the period to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead.

rows.head: Clarke plays hero in overtime
rows.story: Artemi Panarin struck first for the Kings early in the first, and he scored again late in the period to make it 2-0. Logan Stanley and Samuel Helenius fought later in the period. Semyon Varlamov stopped Adrian Kempe on a penalty shot midway through the second.

rows.head: The Flames squeak past the Wild
rows.story: Aydar Suniev and Joel Farabee scored power-play goals a little over three minutes apart midway through the first to put the Flames up 2-0. Michael McCarron cut Calgary’s lead to 2-1 early in the third.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: DiPietro shuts out the Predators
rows.story: The Predators will want to forget this one fast. Casey Mittelstadt got the scoring started for the Bruins early in the first, and Elias Lindholm made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period. David Pastrňák stretched the lead to 3-0 midway through the second.

rows.head: Askarov stands on his head
rows.story: Tim Stützle opened the scoring for the Senators early in the first, but Nolan Allan made it 1-1 for San Jose less than five minutes later. The Sharks’ Igor Chernyshov left late in the period and didn’t return. Tyler Toffoli, Collin Graf and Jacob Trouba scored three goals in just over four minutes midway through the second to put the Sharks up 4-1.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

chips: First goal for a new club
rows.head: Four points for Barron as the Blues beat the Golden Knights
rows.story: Aleksanteri Kaskimäki picked up his first NHL point. Pavel Buchnevich opened the scoring for the Blues on the power play midway through the first. Justin Barron scored his first goal for St.
rows.calls: One of three preview calls held

rows.head: Šilovs slams the door on the Panthers
rows.story: The Panthers’ Cooper Black made his NHL debut in net. Nick Robertson got the scoring started for the Penguins late in the first, and Hendrix Lapierre made it 2-0 midway through the second. Evgeni Malkin stretched the lead to 3-0 early in the third.

rows.head: The Red Wings keep the Canucks winless in nine
rows.story: J.T. Compher was back in the lineup after missing seven games, and picked up an assist. It was a busy first period. Lucas Raymond and William Wallinder scored less than two minutes apart early in the period to put the Red Wings up 2-0.

rows.head: The Devils take down the Ducks
rows.story: Arseny Gritsyuk struck first for the Devils early in the first, his fourth straight game with a goal. Nico Hischier made it 2-0 on the power play late in the period. Tim Washe cut New Jersey’s lead to 2-1 midway through the third, but they got no closer.
rows.calls: Two of four preview calls held

rows.head: Four points for MacKinnon as the Avalanche beat the Lightning
rows.story: Devon Toews and Nazem Kadri scored less than five minutes apart early in the first to put the Avalanche up 2-0. The second period was a wild one. Fedor Svechkov made it 3-0 just 24 seconds into the period, but Jake Guentzel got the Lightning on the board on the power play midway through the period.
rows.calls: One of two preview calls held

rows.head: Cole plays his 1,000th game, but the Blackhawks lose
rows.story: Connor Bedard opened the scoring for the Blackhawks early in the first, but that’s where Chicago’s luck ran out. Jake Evans made it 1-1 for Montréal late in the period, and he struck again shorthanded midway through the second to put the Canadiens ahead 2-1. Kaiden Guhle stretched the lead to 3-1 late in the period.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
rows.story: Both teams come in on a three-game winning streak. At home, Mike Babcock likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Maple Leafs’ third line. The Oilers’ power play has a soft target in the Leafs’ kill.

rows.head: The Sharks’ edge in shots from defensemen
rows.story: The Bruins won the first meeting this season, 6-3 in San Jose. The Bruins are 8-2-1. The Sharks have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Ottawa.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
rows.story: The Rangers come in at 7-4-1, the Senators at 7-4-0. It’s strength against strength: the Rangers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Senators are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Travis Green likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Rangers’ third line.

rows.head: Tuch meets his old team
rows.story: The Sabres come in at 4-4-2, the Capitals at 5-4-0. At home, Spencer Carbery likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Sabres’ first line. The Capitals have the edge over the Sabres on depth.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Red Wings?
rows.story: The Flames have won two in a row. The Red Wings are 4-3-3. The Red Wings shoot a lot, and the Flames give up plenty.

rows.head: Something has to give
rows.story: The Blues have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Vegas. The Hurricanes are 8-2-2. It’s strength against strength: the Hurricanes are near the top of the league for the power play, but the Blues are near the top at the penalty kill.

rows.head: Heavyweight bout
rows.story: The Lightning come in at 7-3-0, the Mammoth at 7-4-0. It’s strength against strength: the Mammoth are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Lightning are one of the best at keeping shots away.

rows.head: Boldy’s favorite opponent
rows.story: The Kraken have won two in a row. The Wild are 6-3-2. At home, Lane Lambert likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Wild’s third line.

rows.head: Special teams lean toward the Golden Knights
rows.story: The Golden Knights come in at 8-4-0, the Blue Jackets at 3-5-0. At home, Rick Bowness likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Golden Knights’ second line. The Knights’ power play has a soft target in the Blue Jackets’ kill.

rows.head: The Devils’ edge in the power play
rows.story: Both teams have won two in a row. At home, Sheldon Keefe likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kings’ third line. The Devils have the edge over the Kings on the power play.

rows.head: The Ducks are searching for answers
rows.story: The Flyers have won three straight. The Ducks are on a five-game losing streak. At home, Rick Tocchet likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Ducks’ fourth line.

rows.head: The Penguins hunt better looks than the Predators
rows.story: The Predators come in at 3-3-3, the Penguins at 4-6-1. At home, Dan Muse likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Predators’ first line. The Penguins wait for good looks, but the Preds settle for hopeful ones.

rows.head: Colton meets his old team
rows.story: The Avalanche come in at 6-4-1, the Predators at 3-3-3. At home, Andrew Brunette likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Avalanche’s first line. The Predators played last night; the Avs are rested.

rows.head: The Panthers hit, the Blackhawks mostly don’t
rows.story: The Panthers come in at 5-4-2, the Blackhawks at 3-7-0. At home, Jeff Blashill likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Panthers’ first line. The Cats hit a lot, but the Blackhawks mostly don’t.

rows.head: The Stars are rolling
rows.story: The Stars have won four straight. The Islanders are 5-3-2. At home, Glen Gulutzan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Islanders’ first line.

rows.head: Something has to change for the Canucks
rows.story: The Canucks are winless in nine (0-8-1). The Wild are 6-3-2. At home, Manny Malhotra likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Wild’s first line.

rows.head: The Jets need a win
rows.story: The Jets are winless in four (0-2-2). The Canadiens are 5-3-2. The Canadiens aren’t the team you remember for chance quality.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Red Wings?
rows.story: The Oilers have won three straight. The Red Wings are 4-3-3. At home, Mike Babcock likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Red Wings’ third line.

rows.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
rows.story: The Rangers are 7-4-1. The Kings have won two in a row. It’s strength against strength: the Rangers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots.

rows.note: Flames shots vs. Maple Leafs D
rows.head: The Flames are going to let it fly
rows.story: The Flames have won two in a row. The Maple Leafs have won three straight. The Flames shoot a lot, and the Maple Leafs give up plenty.

standout.head: Nathan MacKinnon had 4 points
standout.sub: Only 29 other games this season have matched it, moving him from 7th to 3rd.
